newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle light test at $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle light test at $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Friday were slow at $67.00 per cwt in a limited test, feedlot sources said.
About 800 slaughter steers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said. There were no sales in Kansas, they said.
Heavy overnight rainfall that turned to wet snow in the Panhandle made for muddy feedyards, and was seen limiting weight gains until the weather improves by Sunday.
Rainfall was light in the Oklahoma Panhandle and southern Kansas feedlot areas.

Market-ready cattle in the muddy feedyards will need a few days to recover and although rates of gain were seen reduced, the weather was not seen as being severe or widespread enough to raise feedlot cattle prices next week, a Panhandle cattleman said.
Fed cattle prices next week were seen at $67.00 per cwt. Light sales on Thursday pulled prices down $1.00 from the bulk of this week's trade at $68.00.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by weak beef balues amid the heavy pace of this week's slaughter that offset potential support from active retail demand, they said.
Thursday's kill was pegged at 131,000 head, which brought the weekly number to 529,000, compared with 516,000 last week.
